item.title: Tsui Hark at Lumière Festival: ‘We don't know where the future will bring us’
item.description: "We all know that the thing about humanity is that we always fear being replaced by something." Euronews Culture sits down with legendary Hong Kong filmmaker Tsui Hark during this year's Lumière Film Festival.

item.title: Russia arrests Japanese Hokkaido Shimbun journalist on suspicion of spying
item.description: According to Russian security services, he gathered data on "Russia's military readiness" and on mobilised troops and volunteers for the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Prosecution calls Russell Brand 'ruthless' sexual predator at opening of sex assault trial
item.description: Brand is on bail and arrived at court Wednesday to a crowed of photographers and video journalists. He said he felt "blessed."

item.title: MEPs urge EU to shield International Criminal Court from US sanctions
item.description: Lawmakers from across the political spectrum say the EU should activate the Blocking Statute to prevent European companies from complying with measures imposed by the US administration, defined as an "attack by a foreign power."

item.title: How Germany is training medical staff to fight Ebola
item.description: With 9,000 infections and 4,000 deaths, Ebola continues to spread in eastern DR Congo. German experts are training local healthcare workers to treat patients safely and contain the virus.

item.title: EU's methane rules face one-year delay, sparking environmental backlash
item.description: Environmentalists warn that delaying EU methane rules will do little to lower energy prices, accusing Brussels of using energy security and competitiveness to justify weakening the Green Deal.

item.title: Climate change is putting Europe’s brain health at risk
item.description: Rising temperatures, poor air quality and the spread of infectious diseases could increase the burden of neurological disorders, with the most vulnerable communities facing the greatest risks.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 14th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: A new night train will launch between Hamburg and Munich in March 2027
item.description: Nox Mobility’s first night train will link Hamburg and Munich via Bremen and Augsburg, with individual private ‘suites’ for all passengers.

item.title: Portuguese parliament backs extension of parental leave: what changes?
item.description: The new legal framework, arising from a joint proposal by PS and PSD, will give parents a more favourable regime than the one currently in force.

item.title: Iran executes man accused of armed attacks during US-Israeli strikes
item.description: Ali-Sina Mostafavi, 38, a mountaineer and musician from Kerman, was executed on charges of “enmity against God” after being accused of firing on civilians and soldiers during the opening months of the war. He was also charged with participating in the January protests and sending footage

item.title: Former Ukrainian military officer to stand trial in Germany over Nord Stream sabotage
item.description: While some in the West were quick to accuse Russia of sabotaging its own gas export route, German investigators identified a cell of Ukrainians they say were the alleged perpetrators.

item.title: As the US and China race ahead in AI, France carves its own path with Nvidia’s help
item.description: Nvidia bets almost $10 billion in Europe as Paris pushes for AI sovereignty.

item.title: Albania: Student protests in Tirana turn violent as Flamingo Revolution escalates
item.description: Albania's capital, Tirana, saw violent clashes between student protesters and police on Tuesday, 13 October, as demonstrations continued overnight into Wednesday.

item.title: Duane Davis gets minimum 40 years in prison for orchestrating murder of Tupac Shakur
item.description: Shakur was a key figure in a hip-hop rivalry pitting the US East Coast against the West Coast. He was just 25 when he was gunned down in Las Vegas.

item.title: These are the best holiday destinations in Europe for embracing a longevity lifestyle
item.description: Put down the red light masks in favour of walking more, socialising over a glass of wine and eating plant-based food at these longevity hot spots on the continent.

item.title: ASML posts record €11.7 billion in sales but warns it can’t keep up with AI demand
item.description: Dutch equipment supplier ASML warned on Wednesday that its planned supply of machines will not fully meet customers’ AI-driven demand in 2027 and 2028, as it reported record quarterly sales of around €11.7 billion and lifted the lower end of its full-year sales forecast.

item.title: Retro trend: is China simply copying the German VW Beetle here?
item.description: Citroën's 2CV has just been unveiled as an electric car, and the retro Fiat 500 is already a hit. Few know that in China even Germany's VW Beetle is making a comeback, but only in looks.

item.title: Trump faces backlash after posting 'sick' video of UK man killed by tiger
item.description: The man in the real video, identified by the BBC as William Chapman, later died from his injuries following the Saturday incident, police said.

item.title: EU’s AI rules face first enforcement test over lab incidents
item.description: The EU is investigating OpenAI and Anthropic over AI agents that hacked outside organisations, raising questions about whether the AI Act covers rogue models escaping the testing environment.

item.title: Africa records world's fastest gains in disaster resilience, new study shows
item.description: The World Risk Poll, which surveyed 143,000 people across 140 countries, found North Africa up five points and Southern Africa up four, driven by expanding internet access and household preparedness. Yet 220 million people affected by disasters in the past five years received no warning.

item.title: World’s oldest shipwreck discovered off Turkey’s Mediterranean coast
item.description: Archaeologists say a 4,400- to 4,700-year-old shipwreck found near Kekova Island in southern Turkey carried ceramic storage pots and stone anchors across the Mediterranean.

item.title: Storm chaos in Santiago as hail, floods and power cuts slam Chile’s capital
item.description: Heavy rain, hail and thunderstorms flooded Santiago, Chile, on Tuesday, 13 October, disrupting transport and leaving over 36,000 electricity customers without power. Chile’s disaster agency, Senapred, declared a red alert across the Metropolitan Region.

item.title: Turkish police take pro-opposition channel Halk TV off air and arrest 11 in Istanbul raid
item.description: The move came just hours before the start of the defence's arguments in the sprawling corruption trial of jailed Istanbul mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu and some 400 other defendants.

item.title: Denmark’s biggest retailer is training robots for supermarket night shifts. When will they be ready?
item.description: For now, they are slower than supermarket workers, though the start-up says advances in AI will help improve their speed and precision.

item.title: Trump blasts 'not nice' Houthis as attack hits Saudi Aramco facility
item.description: An Aramco building in Dhahran caught fire, and four people were wounded by intercepted missile debris in Riyadh, as Houthi attacks continued after a strike on the capital’s airport killed 13 people in the worst attack on Saudi soil since 2015.

item.title: Ukraine: Russian missiles hit Kyiv homes and power plant, killing 3 and injuring 22
item.description: Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv killed at least three people, injured 22 and damaged homes and power plants, leaving over 600,000 without electricity.

item.title: Starlink terminals operations restricted in Ukraine overnight, adviser to Zelenskyy says
item.description: The development has raised concerns that access to critical American satellite communications could become another source of leverage over Kyiv.

item.title: Ireland's EU budget proposal has no 'weak points', Irish minister says
item.description: Irish Minister of State for European Affairs Neale Richmond has defended Ireland’s proposal for the EU’s next seven-year budget, describing it as a “demonstration of what is actually realistic” amid criticism from other member states.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV recovering from lung cancer surgery: What happens next?
item.description: In the hospital chapel, dozens of faithful prayed for the pope's health during the operation.

item.title: Recent EU-China talks were a 'good starting point', MEP Lange says
item.description: Bernd Lange, S&D MEP and chair of the European Parliament’s International Trade Committee, hopes the EU and China can reach a “comprehensive agreement” to resolve their trade dispute by March next year.

item.title: Trump hails Greenland as 'second to none' for security of US and Europe
item.description: Trump signed a security deal with the leaders of Greenland and Denmark in September, which allows the US to build two military bases in the south and east of the island.

item.title: European Security Council: New idea or a repackaged hybrid toolbox?
item.description: The European Commission wants a European Security Council to counter sabotage and cyberattacks. Critics say it repackages the EU’s existing hybrid toolbox without addressing the unanimity rule that limits its power. Watch the video!

item.title: Oil prices rise after reported Iranian attacks on ships in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Oil prices rose on recent reports that Iran attacked ships in the Strait of Hormuz. European gas prices hovered near a four-year high, while Asian shares had a mixed reaction and European equities opened higher.

item.title: Zelenskyy turns to European allies as Washington wavers
item.description: Good morning, I’m Mared Gwyn. Today: European leaders close ranks with Zelenskyy, drones keep raining on the Black Sea, and an exclusive interview with the Spanish Foreign Minister.

item.title: Taxes, housing and tuition fees: 2027 budget measures impact family budgets in Portugal
item.description: From taxes and wages to pensions, housing and tuition fees, the 2027 State Budget contains several measures that will directly affect household incomes.

item.title: Hospitality is the key: Porto tops ranking as Europe's friendliest city, with Lisbon close behind
item.description: Portuguese hospitality has once again won over international travellers. Porto was voted Europe's friendliest city, with Lisbon second in Condé Nast Traveller readers' ranking.

item.title: Europe Today: Spanish FM on Euronews, Black Sea drone attacks, EU-China reset
item.description: Spain is under pressure on multiple fronts: war in Ukraine, a housing crisis, snap elections, and tension with Morocco over Ceuta. In an exclusive interview, Foreign Minister Albares tells how Madrid is coping. Plus: Drone attacks in the Black Sea, an EU-China reset, and Ireland's EU budget plan.

item.title: Expedia unveils its 2027 destinations of the year – and only two are in Europe
item.description: Just 10 cities and regions made the cut, with South Lake Tahoe in California topping the list ahead of Hyogo in Japan and Punta del Este in Uruguay.

item.title: Gothic getaways, un-adulting and trip snacking: Expedia ‘unpacks’ its top travel trends for 2027
item.description: Travellers will be going full Kate Bush, indulging their inner child and taking shorter breaks in between their bigger holidays next year and beyond.

item.title: FIFA proposes €5.5bn football development fund amid Infantino scrutiny
item.description: The proposal comes as European football leaders seek a candidate to try to unseat Gianni Infantino as FIFA president.

item.title: Money laundering failures land Bank of America with a $1.2 billion fine
item.description: US authorities have imposed a $1.2 billion (€1.07bn) penalty on Bank of America over failures to tackle money laundering. The bank also settled alleged sanctions violations involving Iran and Russia.

item.title: Brian Cox awarded 2026 Stephen Hawking Medal for Science Communication
item.description: British physicist and broadcaster Brian Cox has been awarded the 2026 Stephen Hawking Medal for Science Communication, recognising his work bringing complex scientific ideas to audiences around the world.

item.title: France’s emissions are falling as fuel prices soar. Why is it still missing climate targets?
item.description: Despite using less fossil fuels, France is still far short of the 5 per cent annual reduction in emissions it needs to meet its climate targets.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 14th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 14th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Winter energy bills: Where are gas and electricity prices highest in Europe?
item.description: Household gas and electricity prices have risen less sharply than petrol and diesel prices in Europe. Ahead of winter, Euronews Business compares prices across capital cities and looks at how they have changed since before the Iran war.

item.title: "Global health is a team sport": World Health Summit in Berlin
item.description: In a world of multiple crises, global health must once again be seen as a team sport, says World Health Summit president Prof Dr Axel R. Pries in an interview with Euronews. He also sees Europe, built on the EU framework, in a leading role.

item.title: Ukraine received no intelligence from partners about missiles headed to Kyiv, Zelenskyy says
item.description: Overnight from Monday to Tuesday, Kyiv residents heard explosions from Russian strikes before air raid sirens sounded, something that has occurred only rarely in the past.

item.title: Cornell University suspends frat parties over gang rape allegations
item.description: Cornell has also appointed former US Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to conduct a "comprehensive independent review" of the university's response to the rape allegations.

item.title: Violence in Paris as tens of thousands turn out for student protests across France
item.description: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 11 police officers had been hospitalised following clashes with protesters in Paris on Tuesday.
